To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) Stomatin is a major component of the red cell membrane raft, (b) Stomatin-deficiency results in altered membrane structure and Ca2+-inducible vesiculation.
stomatin is a major determinant of raft-associated actin and that the absence of this association in OHSt cells is associated with a defect in Ca2+-inducible exocytosis.
stomatin is an important component of the membrane raft in erythrocytes and that the deficiency of this protein in OHSt leads to changes in raft structure and function.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structure and function of membrane rafts in the red cell, with the aim of gaining a better understanding of the role of these structures in the pathophysiology of the red cell disorders overhydrated heriditary stomatocytoses (OHSt) and stomatin deficiency (SD).
the role of the protein stomatin in the structure and function of membrane rafts in the erythrocytes of patients with overhydrated hereditaty stomatocytosys.
the structure and function of the erythrocytic membrane, and the role of membrane proteins and cytoskeleton in maintaining the shape, stability and function of the red cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
OHSt is caused by the loss of a protein that has a role in the maintenance of the structure of the erythrocytes plasma membrane and its associated membrane rafts.
the absence of the stomatin protein in the membrane of OHSt cells leads to the loss of a raft-associated actin cytoskeleton and to the production of abnormally large Ca2+-dependent vesicles.
the stomatin protein is essential for the maintenance of membrane raft integrity and that its absence results in membrane raft dysfunction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stomatin is a major determinant of raft structure and that this in turn is important in regulating raft function in the red cell.

stomatin is important in maintaining normal raft-associated actin in the red cell membrane, and that the loss of stomatin from the membrane leads to an increase in raft-associated Ca2+ binding proteins and a decrease in Ca2+ binding stomatin.
the loss of stomatin leads to a reduction in the actin content of membrane rafts, which in turn leads to a reduction of the amount of the membrane skeleton in the rafts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stomatin is an important regulator of raft structure and Ca2+-dependent vesiculation.
stomatin is a key regulator of membrane raft function in erythrocytes and its absence leads to a raft phenotype with altered actin association and Ca2+-dependent vesiculation.

the absence of the raft protein stomatin in OHSt erythocytes leads to the loss of a raft-associated actin network, which in turn leads to a reduction in raft size, a reduction in membrane stiffness, a loss of Ca2+-inducible exovesiculation, and a loss of Ca(2+)-inducible membrane fusion.
